'''Imre Bennett Leader''' (born 30 October 1963) is a British mathematician, a professor in [[DPMMS]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] working in the field of [[combinatorics]]. He is also known as an [[Reversi|Othello]] player.

==Life==
He is the son of the physicist Elliot Leader and his first wife Ninon Neményi (his mother was previously married to the poet Endre Kövesi); [[Darian Leader]] is his brother.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gomori |first1=George |title=Ninon Leader obituary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2022/jan/26/ninon-leader-obituary |work=The Guardian |date=26 January 2022}}</ref> [[Imre Lakatos]] was a family friend and his godfather.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yap Von Bing |title=A Conversation with SMS Distinguished Visitor: Imre Leader |journal=Mathematical Medley |date=December 2013 |volume=39 |issue=2 |page=8 |url=https://sms.math.nus.edu.sg/smsmedley/Vol-39-2/MM%2039_Imre.pdf}}</ref>

Leader was educated at [[St Paul's School (London)|St Paul's School]] in London, from 1976 to 1980.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics at St Paul's |url=https://issuu.com/haimebutler/docs/st-pauls-atrium-autumn_winter2021/s/14071912}}</ref> He won a silver medal on the [[United Kingdom|British]] team at the 1981 [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] (IMO) for pre-undergraduates.<ref>{{IMO results |id=11104 }}</ref> He later acted as the official leader of the British IMO team, taking over from Adam McBride in 1999, to 2001.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bradley |first1=Christopher J. |title=Challenges in Geometry: For Mathematical Olympians Past and Present |date=17 February 2005 |publisher=OUP Oxford |isbn=978-0-19-856691-5 |page=vi |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tM4TDAAAQBAJ&pg=PR6 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=McBride |first1=Adam |title=IMOs I Have Known |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |date=2002 |volume=86 |issue=506 |page=197 |doi=10.1017/S002555720017038X |jstor=3621837 |s2cid=173999479 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3621837 |issn=0025-5572|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="SMS">{{cite web |title=Professor Imre Leader – Singapore Mathematical Society |url=https://sms.math.nus.edu.sg/professor-imre-leader/ |website=sms.math.nus.edu.sg}}</ref> He was the IMO's Chief Coordinator and Problems Group Chairman in 2002.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yap Von Bing |title=A Conversation with SMS Distinguished Visitor: Imre Leader |journal=Mathematical Medley |date=December 2013 |volume=39 |issue=2 |page=2 |url=https://sms.math.nus.edu.sg/smsmedley/Vol-39-2/MM%2039_Imre.pdf}}</ref>

Leader went on to [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], where he graduated B.A. in 1984, M.A. in 1989, and Ph.D. in 1989.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Cambridge |first1=University of |title=Cambridge University List of Members |date=1991 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-42597-1 |page=102 |language=en}}</ref> His Ph.D. in mathematics was for work on combinatorics, supervised by [[Béla Bollobás]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=70125}}</ref> From 1989 to 1996 he was [[Fellow#In ancient universities|Fellow]] at [[Peterhouse, Cambridge]], then was Reader at [[University College London]] from 1996 to 2000. He was a lecturer at Cambridge from 2000 to 2002, and Reader there from 2002 to 2005.<ref name="SMS"/> In 2000 he became a Fellow of Trinity College.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.trin.cam.ac.uk/fellows/master-fellows/ |title=Master and Fellows |publisher=Trinity College, Cambridge}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
In 1999 Leader was awarded a [[Junior Whitehead Prize]] for his contributions to combinatorics. Cited results included the proof, with Reinhard Diestel, of the bounded graph conjecture of [[Rudolf Halin]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Mathematics People |journal=Notices of the AMS |date=November 1999 |page=1239 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199910/people.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Diestel |first1=Reinhard |last2=Leader |first2=Imre |title=A proof of the bounded graph conjecture |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |date=1 December 1992 |volume=108 |issue=1 |pages=131–162 |doi=10.1007/BF02100602 |bibcode=1992InMat.108..131D |s2cid=17240205 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02100602 |language=en |issn=1432-1297|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Othello==
Leader in an interview in 2016 stated that he began to play Othello in 1981, with his friend [[Jeremy Rickard]].<ref>{{cite web |title=WOC 2016 interviews |url=http://othellonews.weebly.com/woc-2016-interviews.html |website=Othello News |language=en}}</ref> In the years from 1982 and 2022 he was 16 times the British Othello champion.<ref>{{cite web |title=Leader wins Nationals for 16th time |url=https://www.britishothello.org/post/leader-wins-nationals-for-16th-time |website=British Othello |language=en |date=24 July 2022}}</ref> In 1983 he came second in the world individual championship, and in 1988 he played on the British team that won the world team championship.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.worldothellofederation.com/historic.asp |title=World Othello Championships |publisher=World Othello Federation |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005065247/http://www.worldothellofederation.com/historic.asp |archivedate=2011-10-05 }}</ref> 

As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, Leader has won the European Grand Prix Championship six times, most recently in 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=European Grand Prix :: World Othello Federation |url=https://www.worldothello.org/about/tournaments/confederate-championships/european-othello-tournaments/european-grand-prix |website=www.worldothello.org}}</ref>
